correctness.rationale: With \(q=T_{k-1}\), the construction has the exact recursion \(T_k=q^4\) and atom \(p_k=q-q^4\). At \(N_k=q^{-4}\), one coordinate has no value above level \(k\) with probability tending to \(e^{-1}\), and conditional on that event its level-\(k\) multiplicity has mean asymptotic to \(q^{-3}=N_k^{3/4}\), so it exceeds \(N_k^{2/3}\) with probability tending to one. Independent coordinate maximizing-index sets of those sizes intersect with probability tending to one, giving the \(e^{-2}\) lower bound. At \(M_k=q^{-3/2}\), each coordinate maximum equals \(k\) with probability tending to one, while the probability of any index satisfying \(X_i=Y_i=k\) is at most \(M_kp_k^2\sim q^{1/2}\to0\). These analytic bounds prove the two subsequences.

originality.rationale: The motivating 2022 primary paper poses the infinite-support independent-coordinate problem and proves \(a_n\to0\) only under a bounded adjacent-atom-ratio hypothesis. The submitted lacunary law deliberately violates that hypothesis and proves a phenomenon not present there: nonconvergence with order-one peaks and zero troughs. The same-author follow-up studies quasi-unidimensional dependent vectors \(f(X)\), not independent product laws. final_claim: There is an explicit infinite-support product law with independent coordinates whose leader probability does not converge: along one subsequence it has liminf at least \(e^{-2}\), while along another it tends to zero.
limitations: The law is deliberately lacunary; exact limsup is not determined and the original no-leader conjecture remains open.
